messages:
Carmen R: Hey team, customer (AcmeAnalytics) reports search quality drop — their semantic search uses embeddings from our hosted env, but results look wrong after they switched a subset to Dedicated. They see lengths/dims mismatch: hosted returns 1536 floats, Dedicated returns 1024.
Carmen R: customer pasted sample: hosted vector length=1536, dedicated vector length=1024. Saying the similarity scores are garbage downstream.
Ben S: thanks, Carmen. Can you paste the exact requests (redact keys) and model ids they used in each env? Also any timestamps for failed requests?
Carmen R: sent in DM: Hosted request used model_id: rwd-embed-large-1536; Dedicated requests target model: rwd-embed-legacy-1024. They say they didn't change code, but the Dedicated endpoint was provisioned by their infra team.
Ben S: ok that already smells like two different model families. But dims shouldn't silently change if you thought you're calling same model id.
Priya N: two quick possibilities: 1) They're accidentally hitting a fallback variant on Dedicated (quantized/legacy) returning 1024; 2) A load-balancer or proxy strip/translate the model param so server picks default model for that pool.
Raj M: also check routing policy and pinned versions. Dedicated pools can have model transforms enabled (auto-quantize). If a pool is configured to 'compat-legacy' we might route to a 1024 variant.
Alice K: Carmen — do we have request/response headers from the customer's Dedicated calls? They may reveal X-Redwood-Model-Variant or X-Redwood-Embed-Dim in metadata.
Carmen R: customer attached logs:
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Host: dedicated.acme.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
{"model":"rwd-embed-large-1536","input":["query text"]}
Response: 200 OK
{"embedding":[... length=1024 ...]}
```

Ben S: interesting — the request model is rwd-embed-large-1536 but response is 1024. That implies server returned a different model variant or post-processed output.
Priya N: we have historical incidents where batcher/quantization pipeline rewrote model to nearest compatible variant if hardware lacks FP32 kernels. Check the Dedicated pool GPU flavor. Was it TI-accelerator with int8-only runtime?
Raj M: checking pool config now — pinging infra. If pool is older and has auto-quantize:true it can replace the backend model with rwd-embed-legacy-1024-quant and emit 1024 dims. We should expose model metadata in response to avoid silent surprises.
deploy-bot: [canary-swap] Canary pool rwd-dedicated-pool-03 had autoscale update applied by @Raj M — change: auto-quantize=true
Alice K: that deploy-bot message lines up with when customer started seeing issues. Carmen — what's the first observed timestamp?
Carmen R: first bad request at 2026-02-20T15:12:03Z (epoch 1719047523). Their reports started around then.
Ben S: ok repro plan: 1) Have support make the same curl against Hosted and Dedicated and capture full JSON response including any "metadata" fields. 2) Call GET /v1/models/<model_id>/metadata against both control plane endpoints to compare reported embedding_dim.
Priya N: also check the batching window/continuous batching on Dedicated. If the batcher merges different model requests into a compatibility path it may pick a lower-dim variant to maximize packing.
Alice K: sample curl to fetch metadata (send to customer):
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models/rwd-embed-large-1536/metadata
# expect JSON with "embedding_dim":1536 and "quantized":false
```

Ben S: customer ran the metadata curl for Dedicated and got: `{"id":"rwd-embed-large-1536","embedding_dim":1024,"variant":"rwd-embed-large-1536-compat-1024-quant"}`
Ben S: so control plane is reporting a compatibility variant. That explains mismatch.
Carmen R: customer also complained they started getting more 429s and occasional 502s after the change, increased retry churn and billing inflation.
Priya N: retries + fallback to compatibility variant could double the number of embed units billed if they retry and each attempt is charged. We should check billing meter for their account between T0 and T1.
Raj M: immediate mitigation: we can force the Dedicated pool to disable auto-quantize or set a strict model allowlist so it won't rewrite to the 1024 variant. I'll open a patch to flip auto-quantize=false for their pool and restart the workers.
Alice K: /assign @Raj M to make the pool change; /cc @Priya N to validate that outputs match Hosted after change.
Raj M: done — changed pool setting and restarted. Watch list: cfg change ID cfg-20260220-443.
deploy-bot: [restarts] Restarted 8 workers in rwd-dedicated-pool-03 by @Raj M — rolling restart started.
Priya N: while rollout is in progress, we should provide a short-term workaround: have customer add header `X-Redwood-Prefer-Variant: strict` to their embedding requests to prefer exact model id (if their SDK supports it). Example: `curl -H "X-Redwood-Prefer-Variant: strict" ...`
Ben S: also ask customer to temporarily pin to model id that we guarantee on Dedicated: `rwd-embed-legacy-1024` or switch all calls to Hosted to keep parity until we fix config.
Carmen R: customer tried `X-Redwood-Prefer-Variant` and reported still 1024 for a few calls but then 1536 returned after restart — looks promising.
Priya N: follow-up checks: 1) confirm embedding_dim in response metadata for a batch of 100 calls; 2) run cosine similarity regression tests on their prompt set to ensure ranking restored; 3) audit logs for retry patterns to refund extra embed units charged if we caused spurious retries.
Raj M: I'll collect worker logs for before/after window and post a link. Also will disable auto-quantize cluster-wide as an opt-out flag for now.
Ben S: FYI, I'm opening a support ticket SUP-2026-2287 and adding logs, billing spike analysis, and the config diff.
Carmen R: customer is asking for ETA to permanent fix and billing remediation. Can we promise an investigation window?
Alice K: commit to 48h for root cause + refund proposal. Priya — you want to own quality validation?
Priya N: yes, I'll run their eval set through Hosted vs Dedicated after change and post numbers.
Ben S: next actions list (short):
- Raj: confirm pool config change & provide logs (cfg-20260220-443).
- Priya: validate embedding_dim parity and ranking on 200 samples.
- Ben: assemble ticket with timeline and ask billing for provisional refund hold.
- Carmen: update customer with workaround header and ETA 48h.
Carmen R: sending update to customer now, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Alice K: marking thread resolved-for-now; please reopen if parity regresses.
